lines.trans: Good morning, me. Hello?
Oh, Miku? You promised you would phone me yesterday, didn't you?

words.gram: Past tense of plain copula だ.

lines.trans: Sorry, sorry — were you already awake?
Long ago! Have you forgotten our family runs a farm?
Honestly, you never call at all. Are you going to your company job properly?
I told you I'm going! Right now I'm saving up my paycheck
because I'd love to gift you a vacation trip, Mom.

words.gram: Past た-form of する (to do/happen).

lines.trans: Thank you, sweetheart — the thought alone is plenty. Are you doing okay for money?
I'm totally fine — my company actually pays a pretty good salary.

words.gram: Na-adjective used here for a polite refusal.

lines.trans: You ran off to Tokyo on your own, and your father worries it's a dangerous city.
There's nothing dangerous at all here, so I'm fine.
Bye for now — I'll call you again soon.

meanings.note: Polite form is おはようございます.

examples.trans: Good morning, did you sleep well?

examples.text: みんなにおはようと言う。

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Signals recognizing someone ('Oh, Toshi!') or letting out a feeling ('Man, I'm hungry').

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Verbal noun; 約束する means 'to promise'.

examples.text: 約束の時間に遅れました。
examples.trans: I was late for the appointment time.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Casual/intimate apology, often softened with な or ね.

meanings.en: to happen; to occur; to wake up
meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.trans: I wake up at seven every morning.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

examples.text: とっくよ。うち農家なの、お忘れ？
examples.trans: Long ago! Have you forgotten our family runs a farm?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Adverb traditionally used with negatives, also used colloquially with affirmatives.

examples.text: 今日は全然寒くないです。
examples.trans: It's not cold at all today.
There is no problem at all.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a business company or one's workplace.

examples.text: 新しい会社に入りました。

examples.trans: The company is near the station.

meanings.note: Reassures that rules or steps are followed properly.

examples.text: ちゃんと確認しました。
ちゃんと並んでいます。

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Conditional particle attached to the hypothetical (e) stem of verbs and adjectives.

examples.text: 練習すれば上手になります。
examples.trans: If you practice, you will get better.
If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

meanings.note: Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

examples.text: お母さんに旅行プレゼントしたいなって思ってんだ。
examples.trans: because I'd love to gift you a vacation trip, Mom.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.note: Used for someone's emotional state or sentiment.
Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Na-adjective stem (also used adverbially).

examples.text: 時間は十分にあります。

meanings.note: Polite/standard form of 金 (かね) with honorific prefix お.
Core everyday reassurance or check covering safety, health, and reliability.

examples.text: 心配しないで、大丈夫だよ。
examples.trans: Do not worry, it is fine.

meanings.note: After なくて (隠さなくて結構です), politely says 'there is no need to'.

examples.text: 明日は来なくて結構です。
examples.trans: You do not need to come tomorrow.

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Humble/plain term for one's own father.

examples.trans: My father is an office worker.
Words I learned from my father.

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Colloquial particle adding emphasis, similar to でも or も.

examples.text: 俺だって言いたいことがある。
examples.trans: I have something I want to say too.

examples.text: 誰だって間違いはある。

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Colloquial particle, often used to downplay or dismiss.

examples.text: テレビなんか見ていないで勉強しろ。
コーヒーなんかどうですか。
examples.trans: How about some coffee or something?

meanings.note: Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。
